sentences: The young hero, after years of training abroad, vows to fight crime in the city in memory of his murdered parents.
While he is initially successful in thwarting robberies, he is disappointed that criminals are unafraid of him and seeks an intimidating disguise.
He also begins a relationship with a woman after they meet at the cemetery while she pays respects to her mother.
Though conflicted about whether to honor his promise to his parents or pursue a happy life with the woman, the hero eventually proposes to her.
However, the woman abruptly leaves the city with her father, a businessman, ending the engagement in a breakup letter.
Heartbroken, the hero commits to a new life as a vigilante crime fighter, converting a cavern under the mansion into a base and assuming the mantle of the vigilante for ten years.
In the present day, the vigilante interrupts a mobster and his associates plotting to launder counterfeit money.
The mobster escapes but dies after crashing his car during a confrontation with the killer, a masked vigilante resembling a grim reaper.
Witnesses see the vigilante at the scene, leading a councilman to vow to have him arrested.
A second mobster visits the first mobster's grave at the cemetery, where he is murdered by the killer, whom the second mobster's bodyguards mistake for the vigilante.
While investigating the scene of the second mobster's death, the vigilante lingers by his parents' grave, where he encounters the woman, who deduces his identity.
The vigilante discovers that the first mobster, the second mobster, and a third mobster were bankrolled by the woman's father.
He interrogates the woman, who claims no knowledge of her father's whereabouts.
After learning of the first mobster's and the second mobster's deaths, the elderly and ailing third mobster fears the vigilante will kill him next.
He seeks help from his former ally, the councilman, but is rebuffed.
In desperation, he turns to the villain, offering him $5 million to kill the vigilante, and reminds him that the killer will be after him next.
The killer goes to confront the third mobster in his penthouse, only to find that he has already been killed by the villain.
Instead of saving the third mobster, the villain rigged a camera to the mob boss's body to identify the mysterious killer.
The villain then remotely triggers rigged explosives, but the killer escapes and avoids capture by the vigilante.
Responding to the blast, the police pursue the vigilante, who eventually eludes them with last-minute help from the woman.
The woman admits to the hero that her father worked for the third mobster and was forced to take her into hiding abroad because he was unable to repay money that he had embezzled from the mob.
Her father later accumulated a fortune and offered to repay the mob, but they refused to lift the hit on him.
The woman says that she returned to the city to stop her father from killing his former partners.
The hero and the woman consider resuming their relationship, despite the hero's uncertainty.
The hero later examines an old photograph of the mobsters and recognizes that the third mobster's enforcer was the villain before his disfigurement.
The villain confronts the councilman, accusing him of ordering the murders to hide his mob connections, but a call from the woman interrupts them and shifts the villain's suspicion onto her.

The councilman is poisoned with the villain's toxin and taken to the hospital, where the vigilante forces him to confess that he previously worked as the woman's family's lawyer and helped them hide from the mob.
The woman's father refused to bankroll the councilman's first struggling election campaign, so the councilman revealed his location to the third mobster in exchange for the mob's support.

The vigilante visits the woman's apartment in her absence and intercepts a message for her from the villain, who implies that he knows that the woman is the killer, then survives the villain's bombing of the apartment.
The vigilante determines that the villain, the now last surviving former member of the third mobster's mob, killed the woman's father on the mob's order and that the woman has gone after him.
The woman confronts the villain at his hideout, the abandoned world's fair, where he attempts to trap and kill her, but she is saved by the vigilante, who unsuccessfully pleads with her to stop.
The villain tries to escape but is incapacitated by the vigilante and surrenders to the woman, who bids the hero farewell before disappearing with the villain as the fair explodes.

The hero survives and is later consoled in the hidden base by the butler, who assures him that he could not have stopped the woman's self-destructive revenge, before discovering that the woman has left her locket containing an old picture of the hero and her as a couple.
The sorrowful woman departs the city on an ocean liner, and the vigilante resumes his watch over the city.
The prelude to the storyline began with the introduction of two new characters key to its storyline in issues prior to the release of the storyline: an assassin, a.k.a.

the student (introduced in issues #1-4 of another title (October 1992-January 1993) by two creators), a graduate student at a university who discovers he has been unconsciously trained since birth as an assassin for an ancient religious order.

The villain, introduced in issue #1 of another title (January 1993) by two creators, an orphan born and raised in an island prison, self-taught and ruthless, who underwent an involuntary experimental operation to become a new type of supersoldier, before breaking free and deciding to take the city from its "king", the vigilante.

The two characters were quickly added to the cast in the monthly titles, with the student being a superhero-in-training who fights alongside the vigilante, while the villain was introduced as a supervillain.

Within the regular series, the buildup to the storyline begins with a six-issue run in issues #484-489 (September 1992 - February 1993), in which the vigilante (at the onset of a personal psychological mid-life crisis) is forced to deal, in rapid succession, with a returning villain and his gang (who target the hero and an associate), a crazed killer, and a sharpshooter assassin hired by an imprisoned mobster to murder the police commissioner.
The vigilante begins to feel that he has lost his edge, especially after his failure to capture the returning villain.
He finds himself unable to meditate or even focus.
As the hero, he contacts a holistic therapist for treatment.
He also assigns his partner to train the student in detective work to aid them as an ally, hoping to guide the student's brainwashing away from making him a villainous threat.

Despite the advice of everyone in his life, including the therapist, the hero refuses to rest and continues to pursue his self-imposed duty despite his worsening condition (although not explicitly noted as a cause, these events take place immediately after the death of a superhero, the vigilante's peer, elsewhere in the shared universe).
In addition, since the events from an earlier story, the vigilante struggles with the trauma of the loss of his protégé.

The next storyline, in issues #654-656 of another title (December 1992 - February 1993), involves a young military student usurping power in the city's underworld and assaulting a police station, with the hero's fatigue continuing to worsen.
At the conclusion of this story, the villain and his henchman are shown monitoring the vigilante's performance.
The villain begins a series of encounters letting the vigilante know of his presence and his intentions.

In issues #489-490 (February–March 1993), the villain interferes with encounters pitting two other villains against the vigilante, and, to test the vigilante's limits, goes so far as to inject one of them with the drug.
This escalation culminates in an assault on the asylum in issue #491 (April 1993), where the villain breaks the inmates free and supplies them with numerous weapons to escape.

Meanwhile, the partner finds it difficult to work with the student, due to the man's violent subconscious training and lack of social skills, and also finds himself being shut out from working alongside the vigilante.
The plot of the storyline begins with the villain freeing all of the maximum-security inmates of the asylum, a notorious psychiatric facility in the city.
Aware that he would lose in a direct assault against the vigilante, the villain's plan consists of weakening the vigilante by forcing him to deal with the escaped villains simultaneously.
The scenario creates a rift in the relationship between the partner and the vigilante, as the vigilante irrationally seeks to face the outbreak alone.
Over the next few issues, the vigilante becomes weaker and weaker as each criminal is put away.

The rescue of the mayor from the teaming of two villains pushes the vigilante to his mental and physical limits: a dose of one of the villains' fear gas makes him relive the murder of his protégé, which he considers to be his greatest failure.

After this encounter, the villain's men assault the vigilante before he himself makes his move and attacks him at the mansion, his home as his alter-ego—long before this time, the villain had deduced the secret identity of the vigilante.
The fight between the hero and the villain is detailed in issue #497.
After three months, the exhausted vigilante was no match for the villain; the villain pummels him ruthlessly before breaking the vigilante's back, symbolically "breaking" the vigilante.
The villain takes the vigilante downtown to the city square and throws him from a rooftop to demonstrate his superiority to the populace.
Quick action by the partner and the butler spares the vigilante's life, but he is left paraplegic.
The hero uses a special wheelchair created by an ally.
With the vigilante incapacitated, the villain assumes control of the city's underworld and takes over several illegal operations within it.
After his defeat, the hero enlists the aid of the therapist to rehabilitate him and asks the student to take up the mantle of the vigilante so that the city has a protector.
Soon after, the therapist and the partner's father are kidnapped and the hero and the butler leave the country to find them.

The student is shown to be a different, but not dangerous, vigilante until an encounter with another villain, which results in the student being infected by that villain's fear gas and his conditioning—his programming as an assassin—taking over, in order to combat the student's fear.

Following this, the student is unable to shake the influence of the conditioning, giving in to it completely after his first defeat at the villain's hands and being increasingly influenced by it during the rest of his tenure as the vigilante.
Gradually, the student alienates the partner with his paranoia and arrogance.

In issue #500, the student, in his new mechanical suit (which is an amalgam of the assassin's costume and the vigilante's), confronts the villain in an arduous battle and prevails, although many bystanders are put at risk.
The student leaves the villain broken mentally and physically, though he struggles with the choice of whether to simply kill the villain or hand him over to the police.
He decides that he will let the villain go to prison.
The student continues to watch over the city after the fight, but grows increasingly unstable.
At the onset of the next storyline, the student has been established as the vigilante, and the hero is out of the country.
Instead of a crossover with a definite ending, the publishers treated the scenario as though it were the new status quo, leaving it open-ended.
In the city, the vigilante defuses a hostage situation orchestrated by the criminal, formerly the district attorney, who escapes.
Flashbacks reveal that the criminal, once one of the vigilante's biggest supporters, was horribly disfigured with acid on one side of his face by a mobster.

The trauma of the incident caused the criminal to develop a split personality, make decisions based on the flip of a coin, and swear vengeance against the vigilante for failing to prevent the incident.

The inventor, an eccentric and egotistical researcher at the company, approaches his employer, the hero, to present an invention that can beam television signals directly into the brain, demanding immediate approval directly from the hero.
The hero rejects the device as he is concerned that the technology could manipulate minds.
After killing his abusive supervisor and staging it as a suicide, the inventor resigns and plots revenge against the hero, sending him riddles.
A criminal psychologist diagnoses the inventor as psychotic.
The hero attends a circus with the psychologist.
The criminal hijacks the event and threatens to detonate a bomb unless the vigilante reveals his identity.

The acrobat, the youngest member of a family of acrobats, prevents the bomb from killing anyone by throwing it into a river with the help of his family; however, the criminal kills all of them except the acrobat in the process.
The hero invites the now-orphaned acrobat to live at the mansion as his ward, where he later discovers that the hero is the vigilante.

Seeking to avenge the death of his family, the acrobat demands to join the vigilante in crime-fighting, hoping to kill the criminal, but the hero declines in order to help the acrobat move on instead, as he is considering retirement.
The inventor becomes a villain and teams up with the criminal.

They commit a series of robberies to finance the inventor's new company and mass-produce his brainwave device, which steals information from minds and transfers it to the inventor's, increasing his intelligence but also slowly causing him to lose his grip on reality.
At a party hosted by the inventor, the vigilante pursues the criminal and is almost killed until the acrobat saves him.
The vigilante visits the psychologist, who explains that she has fallen in love with the hero, and the hero reveals his secret identity to her.
Having discovered the hero's secret through the device, on Halloween night, the criminal and the inventor destroy the hidden base, shoot the hero, and abduct the psychologist.
As the hero recovers, he and his butler deduce that the inventor is the villain through clues he left in his riddles, while the psychologist is held prisoner in the inventor's lair.
The hero finally accepts the acrobat as his comrade, his partner.
At the inventor's lair, the acrobat defeats the criminal but chooses to spare him, which allows the criminal to capture the acrobat at gunpoint.

The inventor reveals his final riddle: the psychologist and the acrobat, representing the two sides of the vigilante's personality, are trapped in tubes above a deadly drop, and he only has the time to save one.

The vigilante distracts the inventor with a riddle himself, before destroying the inventor's brainwave receiver with a weapon, damaging the inventor's mind and enabling the vigilante to rescue both when he sees the floor is an optical illusion.
The criminal corners them and flips his coin to decide their fate, but loses his balance after the vigilante throws multiple identical coins in the air, and falls to his death.
Committed to the asylum, a now-delusional inventor exclaims that he is the vigilante.
The hero, the real vigilante, resumes his crusade with the acrobat as his partner.
At a wedding in June, the city's mob boss tries to pressure the hero to help launder his money, but the hero refuses.
Later, the hero (as the vigilante) returns to investigate the mob boss's penthouse but finds a woman similarly engaged.
The vigilante meets with the district attorney and a police captain.
The three agree to a pact to end the mob boss's crime reign, bending but never breaking the law to achieve it.
The hero, on the board of the city bank, uses his sway and influence as the vigilante to oust the current president and take over to rid the bank of its mob money.
Under orders from his uncle, the mob boss's nephew assassinates the bank president.
The nephew himself is killed on Halloween by an unknown assailant, leaving behind an untraceable pistol, a nipple from a baby bottle used as a crude silencer, and a jack-o-lantern.
The woman leads the vigilante to a warehouse where the mob boss has been forced to stash his funds.
The vigilante and the district attorney set the warehouse on fire to destroy the money.
The mob boss responds by hiring a family, a gang of Irish hitmen led by the head of the family, to destroy the district attorney's home with a bomb, but he and his wife survive.
On Thanksgiving, the hitmen themselves are killed by an unknown agent who leaves the same type of pistol and silencer behind, along with a Thanksgiving decoration.
The killer is given a nickname by the media.
The mob boss's bodyguard is killed similarly on Christmas.
The killer is believed to be a rival of the mob boss's family.
On New Year's Eve, the vigilante stops a villain from using deadly laughing gas to kill everyone in the city square.
Meanwhile, the district attorney's corrupt assistant finds evidence supposedly linking the mob boss to the hero.
Aboard the mob boss's yacht, the mob boss's son is killed by the killer on New Year's Eve.
Over the next few months, the killer's targets change to that of a rival crime gang in the city.
A war between the mob boss's family and the rival gang breaks out, and the mob boss is forced to turn to enlist the city's "freaks" (such as four villains) to hold his ground.
Per the mob boss's instructions, a villainess ensnares the hero on Valentine's Day, coercing him into laundering money for the mob boss.
This unintentionally takes the vigilante out of the equation.
It is not until Saint Patrick's Day that the woman figures out what has happened to him and, in costume, frees him from the villainess's clutches.
One villain becomes the first target to be spared by the killer on April Fool's Day, which the vigilante comes to suspect as being a message from the killer to the mob boss.
Meanwhile, the pistols left behind by the killer and the bullets gleaned from the killer's victims are traced to a neighborhood, but the gunmaker is found dead as the killer's victim on Mother's Day.

On the following day, the district attorney follows up on the assistant's investigation and has the hero arrested, claiming that as the hero's father saved the mob boss's life after he was shot, that the hero is loyal to the mob boss's family.

However, the hero's butler testifies that the hero's father's report never came to light due to police corruption, which helps declare the hero innocent, especially in light of the murder of the city coroner on Independence Day.
The rival gangster, having been arrested earlier, offers to testify against the mob boss after his father is killed on Father's Day.
During the trial, he throws a vial of acid—secretly given to him earlier by the assistant—at the district attorney, disfiguring half of the district attorney's face.
The district attorney is rushed to a hospital but escapes into the sewers, befriending a stranger when he encounters him.
The police captain deduces the district attorney may be the killer, but the vigilante refuses to believe it until he can talk to the district attorney himself.
After the mob boss's sister is murdered on the mob boss's birthday in August, the vigilante questions a criminal on where to find the district attorney.
The criminal suggests that, since it is Labor Day, the killer will try to kill the rival gangster.
The vigilante stages a plan with the police captain to move the rival gangster, giving the killer the means and opportunity.
During the transfer, the killer murders the rival gangster, but the vigilante – having disguised himself as one of the security guards – takes him down.
The killer is revealed to be the son of the mob boss, who had faked his death.
On Halloween, the district attorney resurfaces as a villain.
He releases most of the super-criminals from the asylum, then seeks out and kills both the mob boss and the assistant, despite the vigilante's attempts to stop him.
The mob boss's daughter is also apparently killed in a struggle with the woman.
His revenge complete, the villain turns himself in to the police captain and the vigilante but tells them that there were two killers.
The police captain is confused, as the son has already confessed to all of the killings.
The vigilante and his partner encounter a new villain, who has left a string of diamond thefts in his wake.
During a confrontation at the natural history museum, the villain steals a diamond and flees, freezing the partner to distract the vigilante.
Later, the vigilante and his partner learn that the villain was originally a doctor, a scientist working to develop a cure for a disease, hoping to heal his wife.
After a lab accident, the villain was rendered unable to live at average temperatures and forced to wear a cryogenic suit powered by diamonds for survival.
At a company lab abroad, a botanist is working under a supervisor, who has turned her research on plants into a super soldier serum.
After witnessing the supervisor use it to mutate a serial killer into a super soldier, she threatens to expose the supervisor's experiments.

The supervisor attempts to kill her by overturning a shelf of various toxins; instead, the botanist is mutated by the toxins into a villainess, who murders the supervisor with a venom-laden kiss, destroys the lab, and escapes to the city with the super soldier, plotting to use the hero's money to support her research.
Meanwhile, the butler's niece makes a surprise visit and is invited by the hero to stay at the mansion until she goes back to school.
The company presents a new telescope for the observatory at a press conference interrupted by the villainess.
She proposes a project that could help the environment, but the hero declines her offer, knowing it could leave the impoverished without food or heating.
The vigilante and his partner decide to lure the villain out using the hero's family diamonds and present them at a company charity event.
The villainess attends the event and uses her abilities to seduce the vigilante and his partner.
The villain crashes the party but is defeated and incarcerated at the asylum.
The villainess takes an interest in the villain and helps him escape with the super soldier’s help, killing two guards with her kiss in the process.

The partner discovers that the niece has been participating in drag races to raise money for the butler, who is dying of the disease; a fact he kept from the hero and the partner, but his niece is secretly aware of his situation and is trying to find treatment for him.

The vigilante, his partner, and the police arrive at the villain's lair in response to his escape, discovering his wife preserved in a cryogenic chamber and that the villain has developed a cure for the early stages of the disease.
The rogues soon secretly arrive to recover the villain's diamonds and his wife.

Wanting the villain for herself, the villainess cuts the power to his wife's chamber, steals the diamonds, and seduces the partner and nearly kisses the partner, escalating tensions between him and the vigilante.
At her hideout, the villainess lies to the villain that the vigilante killed his wife, manipulating him to help her in her quest to repopulate the planet using her mutant plants afterward.
The villain and the super soldier commandeer the observatory and convert the new telescope into a giant freeze ray, while the villainess uses the signal light to contact the partner.
The partner attempts to go after the villainess alone, but the vigilante convinces him not to fall for the villainess's seduction, giving him a pair of rubber lips to survive her deadly kiss.
The niece discovers the hidden base, where an artificial intelligence version of the butler reveals he has made a suit for the niece.
The niece becomes a heroine, arriving at the villainess's lair in time to save the vigilante and his partner from the villainess.
The villain begins to freeze the city over while the vigilante, his partner, and the heroine head to the observatory together to stop him.
The vigilante defeats the villain in combat, while the heroine and the partner drain the super soldier's serum and thaw the city.
The villain accuses the vigilante of taking his wife's life, only to be shown a recording of the villainess admitting to the crime.
The vigilante reveals that the villain's wife survived and offers the villain the chance to continue his research on the disease in exchange for his cure.
The villain accepts and returns to the asylum, where he is imprisoned in the same cell as the villainess, whom he plans to torment.
The butler is cured, and the hero and the partner agree to let the niece join them in fighting crime.

A new faction of the gang—consisting of four members and a pair of twins—attempts to steal high-tech electronic equipment but is intercepted by the vigilante (the hero), protégé of the original vigilante, the mentor.
The gang reports to their leader, the villain—presumed dead for four decades—who shoots one member to intimidate the surviving members.
Later, the gang disrupt a press conference celebrating the mentor's return to the company to steal equipment.
During the raid, the villain reveals himself to the mentor, mocking his stupefaction and implying that he knows the mentor was the vigilante.
After fending off the attack, the hero demands information from the mentor and the police commissioner, a former heroine, but neither gives him the answers he seeks.
Not wanting the hero to face the villain, the mentor orders him to return the suit.
The hero argues that being the vigilante makes him a personal exemplar, but the mentor rebukes him, comparing him to his former mentees.
Later, the gang ambush the hero and nearly kill his girlfriend.
Meanwhile, the villain poisons the mentor and his Great Dane, verifying that he knows all of their secrets.

After the hero saves the mentor's life with an antidote, the police commissioner finally explains the villain's disappearance: After an ally had left the city for another city, the villain and his accomplice kidnapped the former sidekick, then the sidekick and took him to the abandoned asylum, where they tortured and drugged him for three weeks.
After the villain learned the vigilante's secret identity, he warped the former sidekick into his teenage facsimile, scheming for the sidekick to kill the vigilante.

After the vigilante and the heroine found the former sidekick, a battle ensued, during which the former sidekick briefly came to his senses and killed the villain instead, while the accomplice fell down a ravine and was presumed dead.
They buried the villain beneath the asylum, and only the police commissioner's father and predecessor knew of the incident.

Over the next year, the former sidekick recovered with help from the mentor's family friend, but was forced to retire from superheroics by the latter, and severed ties with him, leaving to make it on his own.

As the vigilante, the hero visits the former sidekick, now a successful telecommunications engineer with a family, who voices bitterness towards his past but denies involvement in the villain's return.
The hero's next suspect is an executive of the company who hates the mentor for ruining his chance to take over the company.
He finds that the executive is not the villain but had conspired with him to kill the mentor.
When a directed-energy weapon strikes the executive's yacht, the hero rescues him before turning him over to the police.
In the hidden base, after realizing the villain only destroyed the sidekick costume, the hero recalls the former sidekick's grudge against his old persona and deduces he must be involved.

Cross-referencing the former sidekick's telecom expertise with the gang's thefts, the hero and the mentor discover that their stolen equipment can assemble an uplink-jammer that seizes control of a laser-armed military satellite.
When the hero goes to face the former sidekick in his workplace, he triggers a trap set by the villain, whom he follows to an abandoned candy factory.

Subduing the gang with the dog's help, the hero confronts the former sidekick, who subdues the hero by disabling his suit and then transforms into the villain as the mentor watches in horror from the hidden base through the hero's suit.

The villain reveals that he encoded his himself into an advanced, stolen DNA microarray hidden behind the former sidekick’s ear—a contingency plan in case he didn't survive his final battle with the vigilante.
This biotechnology allows him to survive death by taking over the former sidekick's body permanently.
Since his return, the villain has plotted a devastating victory over the vigilante.
He aims to use the satellite to kill the mentor and the hero's loved ones before decimating the city.
Leveraging the mentor's insight that the villain is driven by vanity, the hero taunts the villain during their battle, forcing him to drop his guard and play by the hero's rules.
The enraged villain uses his grenades to blast the hero down from the rafters, pins him down to deliver the killing blow.
The hero seizes the opportunity to press the villain's own lethal joy buzzer against the biochip, destroying the villain's digitized code.
He and the dog then rescue the unconscious former sidekick as the lair explodes.
Following the gang's arrests, the police commissioner hides the former sidekick's complicity to protect him while the villain is declared dead.
The twins are bailed out of jail by their grandmother, the elderly, reformed accomplice, who survived the fall.
While the former sidekick recovers in the hospital, the mentor finally makes amends with him and the police commissioner.
Together, they validate the hero's worthiness of the vigilante legacy, acknowledging his courage against the villain.
The vigilante is rescuing a boy kidnapped and held hostage by a kidnapper when a thief steals the ransom money.
As the vigilante swings through the city in pursuit of her, his grapple is cut and he falls to the ground, fracturing his skull.
He is nearly killed by a group of criminals before he is saved by a heroine.
His butler follows his instructions to summon the hero's childhood friend, who is now a renowned brain surgeon.
The surgeon removes the skull fragments from the hero's brain.
The vigilante recovers and discovers that a villainess used the thief to steal the ransom before taking the money from her.
The thief is furious after learning that the villainess had used mind-control powers on her.
The vigilante rescues the thief and a romance blooms between them.
The vigilante eventually decides to trust the thief and reveals his identity to her.
At this time, the kidnapper's increasing savageness due to his condition mutating allows him to escape from the asylum, with the vigilante tracking him.
The kidnapper leads the vigilante to one of the villainess's abandoned greenhouses.
Before he can interrogate him further, the kidnapper is captured.
The vigilante and the thief track the villainess to another city.
There, the villainess has taken control of a superhero and commands him to kill the vigilante.
The vigilante observes that the superhero is subconsciously resisting the villainess's influence, holding back in his attempts to kill.

Using various weapons, including flashbang grenades, hypersonics, electroshock, and a ring of the green rock to defend himself, the vigilante stalls the superhero while the thief lets a woman fall from a building.
The superhero breaks free of the villainess's control to save the woman; he and the vigilante then capture the villainess.
Later, in the city, the hero, the thief, a friend, and the surgeon are attending the opera, when an accomplice tries to rob everyone in the theater.
In the ensuing struggle, the surgeon is apparently shot dead by the villain.
Enraged, the vigilante begins to brutally beat the villain, knocking out the accomplice and even the thief in the process when they tried to intervene.
The vigilante attempts to kill the villain but is then dissuaded by the former police commissioner, who intervenes by superficially wounding the vigilante with a gunshot.
An ally returns to the city for the surgeon's funeral.
The vigilante tells him of his suspicions that some mastermind is behind all his enemies behaving so out of character.
Behind the scenes, a man with a bandaged face appears at all of the crime scenes, and seems to be orchestrating the plot.
He comes to be referred to by a nickname.
After foiling an armored car robbery by another villain, the ally and the vigilante discover evidence that another enemy is also involved in what the vigilante has come to think of as a grand plot.
The vigilante kidnaps the enemy's daughter and leaves the thief to guard her while he seeks out the enemy, who reveals that someone from the hero's past has used one of the pits.
The thief is overpowered by an attacker who has been sent to rescue the daughter, but the daughter knocks the attacker out and helps the thief recover from the attack.
Returning to the city, the vigilante finds the thief being attacked by the delusional heroine.
The vigilante manages to have her knocked out.
He then encounters the cause of the heroine's attack, another villain, but overpowers him in a graveyard.
He discovers that the current sidekick has been captured by the former second sidekick, who had previously perished.
In the ensuing fight, it becomes apparent that an impostor is mimicking the identity of the second sidekick.
The vigilante then finds a device planted in his computer, which lead him to seek his old friend (and trusted mechanic).
He has a late-night meeting with the mechanic, who has been missing for some time.
The mechanic admits that someone had treated his disfigured condition in exchange for planting that device, but he is shot and killed by the bandaged man before he can name the mastermind.

The surgeon is discovered to be the trigger-man, and the face behind the bandages of the mastermind (it is later implied that the impostor had been mimicking the surgeon when he appeared to be killed).

The surgeon held a grudge against the hero's family since the vigilante's father, a doctor, had saved the life of the surgeon's mother after a motor vehicle accident; the surgeon had sabotaged his parents' vehicle in order to gain their inheritance, and considered the hero's father as the one who did not allow his plan to be completed.
In the ensuing confrontation, the surgeon is shot by a reborn criminal and plummets into the water, with the vigilante never having a chance to unmask him (it is only assumed it is the surgeon).
His body is unable to be recovered.
In the city, the young hero falls down a well and develops a fear of bats.
One evening, the hero visits the opera with his parents; the performers masquerading as bats upset him, and he asks to leave.
As the family leave the theater, a mugger attempts to rob the hero's parents and shoots them dead.
A police officer comforts the orphaned hero.
The city police capture the mugger, who is sent to prison for his crime.
The hero is raised by the family butler.
Fourteen years later, the mugger testifies against a mafia crime boss, and is paroled.
The hero intends to murder the mugger to avenge his parents, but an assassin in the crime boss's employ kills him first.
The hero's childhood friend confronts him about his desire for vengeance.

After confronting the crime boss, who says real power comes from being feared, the hero spends the next seven years traveling the world, training in combat, and immersing himself in the criminal underworld.
In a foreign prison, the hero is approached by a recruiter, who recruits him into an order, led by its leader.
The recruiter trains the hero to conquer his fear using a hallucinogenic compound derived from the mountain's blue flowers.
After completing his training, the hero rejects the order's mandate for capital punishment and learns they plan to destroy the city, which the leader believes is corrupt beyond saving.
The hero escapes after burning the order's temple; the leader is killed by falling debris, while the hero saves an unconscious recruiter.
Intent on fighting crime and redeeming the city, the hero returns to the city, the butler, and his family's company, which is being taken public by a businessman.
The company archivist, a friend of the hero's father, allows him access to prototype defense technologies, including a protective bodysuit and an armored vehicle.
Finding the well from his childhood, the hero explores further, discovering a vast cave underneath the mansion.
The hero poses publicly as a shallow playboy while taking up a vigilante identity, inspired by his childhood fear.

Intercepting a drug shipment, the vigilante provides the friend, now an Assistant District Attorney, with evidence against the crime boss and enlists a sergeant, one of the city's few honest police officers, to arrest him.
In prison, the crime boss meets with a doctor, a corrupt psychologist with whom the crime boss has been smuggling drugs into the city.
The crime boss threatens to inform the police about a secret compound in the drugs unless the psychologist's mysterious employer cuts a deal with him.
Donning a scarecrow mask, the psychologist sprays the crime boss with a fear-inducing hallucinogen, driving him insane.
While investigating the psychologist, the vigilante is sprayed with the hallucinogen.
He awakens on his birthday, having been saved by the butler and the archivist, who developed an antidote for the toxin.
The friend confronts the psychologist, who reveals the drug has been introduced into the city's water supply and gives her a potentially lethal dose.
The vigilante captures the psychologist, who claims to work for the leader.
Evading the police in the armored vehicle, the vigilante saves the friend and administers the archivist's antidote.
He gives her two antidote vials: one for the sergeant, and one for mass production.
At the hero's birthday party, the recruiter reveals himself as the true leader, who employed the psychologist to weaponize the order's blue flower compound.

Having stolen a powerful microwave emitter from the company, the leader plans to vaporize the city's water supply, rendering the psychologist's drug airborne and causing mass hysteria that will destroy the city.
He burns down the mansion, but the butler rescues the hero.
The order releases the psychologist and the other asylum inmates into a poverty-ridden district of the city.
The friend enters the district and finds the sergeant, but the police isolate the district.
The leader loads the emitter onto the city's monorail to release the drug at the city's central water source under the company's tower.
The friend is attacked by the psychologist but fends him off with a taser.
As the gas strikes the district, the friend, the inoculated sergeant, and the vigilante struggle to survive.
The vigilante reveals his identity to the friend before fighting the leader on the train.
The sergeant uses the armored vehicle's cannons to destroy the monorail's track and the vigilante glides from the train as it derails and crashes, killing the leader.
The friend now respects the hero but refuses to be with him, promising they can be together when the city no longer needs the vigilante.
The vigilante becomes a public hero.
A gang of masked criminals rob a mafia-owned bank in the city, betraying and killing each other until the sole survivor, the villain, reveals himself as the mastermind and escapes with the money.
The vigilante, the district attorney, and a police lieutenant ally to eliminate the city's organized crime.

The vigilante's true identity, the billionaire, publicly supports the district attorney as the city's legitimate protector, believing the district attorney's success will allow him to retire as the vigilante and romantically pursue his childhood friend—despite her being with the district attorney.
The city's mafia bosses gather to discuss protecting their organizations from the villain, the police, and the vigilante.
The villain interrupts the meeting and offers to kill the vigilante for half of the fortune their accountant concealed before fleeing abroad to avoid extradition.
With the help of the company's CEO, the vigilante finds the accountant abroad and returns him to the custody of the city police.
His testimony enables the district attorney to apprehend the crime families.
The bosses accept the villain's offer, and he kills high-profile targets involved in the trial, including the judge and the police commissioner.
Although the lieutenant saves the mayor, the villain threatens that his attacks will continue until the vigilante reveals his identity.
He targets the district attorney at a fundraising dinner and throws the friend out of a window, but the vigilante rescues her.
The billionaire struggles to understand the villain's motives, to which his butler says that "some men just want to watch the world burn."
The district attorney claims he is the vigilante to lure the villain out, who attacks the police convoy transporting the district attorney.
The vigilante and the lieutenant apprehend the villain, and the lieutenant is promoted to commissioner.
At the police station, the vigilante interrogates the villain, who says he finds the vigilante entertaining and has no intention of killing him.
Having deduced the vigilante's feelings for the friend, the villain reveals she and the district attorney are being held separately in buildings rigged to explode.
The vigilante races to rescue the friend while the lieutenant and the other officers go after the district attorney, but they discover the villain has given their positions in reverse.
The explosives detonate, killing the friend and severely burning the district attorney's face on one side.
The villain escapes custody, extracts the fortune's location from the accountant, and burns it, killing the accountant in the process.
A consultant for the company deduces and tries to expose the vigilante's identity, but the villain threatens to blow up a hospital unless the consultant is killed.

While the police evacuate hospitals and the lieutenant struggles to keep the consultant alive, the villain meets with a disillusioned district attorney, persuading him to take the law into his own hands and avenge the friend.
The district attorney defers his decision-making to his now half-scarred, two-headed coin, killing the corrupt officers and the mafia involved in the friend's death.
As panic grips the city, the villain reveals that two evacuation ferries, one carrying civilians and the other prisoners, are rigged to explode at midnight unless one group sacrifices the other.
To the villain's disbelief, the passengers refuse to kill one another.
The vigilante subdues the villain but refuses to kill him.
Before the police arrest the villain, he says that although the vigilante proved incorruptible, his plan to corrupt the district attorney has succeeded.
The district attorney takes the lieutenant's family hostage, blaming his negligence for the friend's death.
He flips his coin to decide their fates, but the vigilante tackles him to save the lieutenant's son, and the district attorney falls to his death.

Believing the district attorney is the hero the city needs, and the truth of his corruption will harm the city, the vigilante takes the blame for his death and actions, persuading the lieutenant to conceal the truth.

The butler burns an undelivered letter from the friend to the billionaire that says she chose the district attorney, and the CEO destroys the invasive surveillance network that helped the vigilante find the villain.
The city mourns the district attorney as a hero, and the police launch a manhunt for the vigilante.
The story begins with the vigilante and his partner perched onto a gothic building lit by lightning, where the former defiantly proclaims, "The vigilante and his partner will never die!".
Events then flash back to the city six months earlier, where a club leader announces his club's next venture: the destruction of the vigilante.
The hero is dating a model who is very influential in her home country.
The model discovers the hero was the vigilante relatively early in their relationship, and the revelation makes the relationship easier for the hero to handle.
He lets the model so deep into his life that he even introduces her to the hidden base.
Meanwhile, a club member contacts the villain in the asylum and offers him a role in their assault on the vigilante.
The model tries to convince the vigilante that he is simply living a life he has fabricated in his own head as a child to cope with the death of his parents.
This suggestion begins to affect the vigilante's already-strained psyche, and he passes out when the model says aloud a word that was on all the computer's screens: the code word.
As he passes out, the leader and minions of his diabolical club infiltrate the hidden base.
They drug the vigilante, beat the butler, and wreak havoc upon the cave.
When the hero is seen next, he wakes up in a pile of garbage with no memory of himself.
He meets a homeless man, who recognizes that the hero is going through drug withdrawal and helps him.
As the two spend time together, traveling in what the homeless man calls an "odyssey" across the city, the hero sees more evidence of his forgotten life.
The two reflect on the day, and the homeless man gives the hero an old broken radio as a sentimental gift.

Abruptly, the hero finds that the homeless man is no longer sitting next to him and learns from a local dealer that the homeless man had blown two hundred dollars on heroin and overdosed the previous day.
This statement devastates the hero and further confuses his sense of reality.
At this point, the hero seems to snap.
He makes himself a costume out of red, yellow, and purple rags, and begins referring to the broken radio by a nickname.
He then calls himself by a new vigilante name and begins taking advice from a companion.

His new persona hunts down and dispatches two small-time members of the club, and finds that his next destination is the asylum, armed with nothing but a baseball bat, his radio, and miscellaneous bits of junk that serve in place of his utility belt.
The vigilante and the companion ultimately make it to the asylum, where the companion says he cannot follow.
Inside, the vigilante is confronted by the villain, who holds the model captive and kills her in front of him using the flowers that make up the villain's laughing gas.

As the vigilante regains his sanity and loses consciousness from the same poisonous flowers, the model appears to be okay, the villain is smiling, the leader is there, and everyone is asking the vigilante "Now do you get it?"
It is revealed that the model has been a part of the club all along.
The code word was written all over the city by the leader as a subliminal trigger to be used when the time was right to break the vigilante's mind.
The leader calls off the villain, referring to him as "my good and faithful servant".
The straitjacketed vigilante is buried in a shallow grave, the leader's intention being to exhume him once oxygen deprivation has permanently damaged his mind.
Back in the asylum, the villain murders a club member and places a bet with those who remain: that the vigilante will emerge from the grave undamaged and hunt them down, as he always does.
While the now mentally stable vigilante escapes the shallow grave that the club put him in, the villain points out that no one has investigated the vigilante's radio.
When they do, they activate a transmitter that brings an ally, the vigilante's partner, another ally, and a band of assassins right to them.
Before the villain flees in an ambulance, he promises the remaining club members that he will collect his winnings from them soon and tells the leader that he should not have called him his servant.
The vigilante hunts down the leader, who tries to convince the hero that he is his father, but the vigilante believes him to be a different man, an actor who had once been his father's double.
As the leader tries to escape, the vigilante infiltrates his escaping helicopter, causing it to crash in a blazing explosion.
Flying back to her own country, the model's plane is ambushed by a third party's commandos.

Back in the present-day city, the club member tells his henchmen that the vigilante has not been seen in months and that they are free to commit crimes unmolested, when suddenly a signal-like light comes on above them, bringing the story full circle to its opening image.
In the epilogue, the young hero is walking home with his parents after seeing a movie.
The hero wonders what it would be like if the movie's hero showed up.
The hero's father responds, "The sad truth is, they'd probably throw someone like the movie's hero in the asylum", as he notices someone in front of them.
